question: 在公开官方一手资料范围内，Gemini CLI 的任务生命周期、权限边界、审计/可观测性、取消、超时与失败恢复分别能被证明到什么程度？

scope.time_window: current as of 2026-09-22; repository main commit d5b3e3accb26000d273abf16e0f1dd83aa5428a9
exclusions: shared/P0, incident, D10/L12/D14, canonical, 140, tri-line, systemd, old S1/S2/S3 directories

claims.claim: Tool-call lifecycle has validating, scheduled, executing, awaiting_approval and terminal success/error/cancelled states; scheduler validates then executes then finalizes.

sources.support: CoreToolCallStatus and typed call variants define states and terminal union.
Scheduler code processes validating, scheduled execution, terminal finalization.

claims.caveat: This is tool-call lifecycle, not a durable whole-user-task protocol.

claims.claim: Plan Mode is read-only by default, allows only specified read/research tools and plan Markdown writes, and requires human plan approval/iteration; YOLO blocks Plan transitions.

sources.support: Official Plan Mode guide states read-only restrictions, plan review, approve/iterate/cancel and YOLO restriction.
Catch-all deny plus explicit read-only and plan-file exceptions.
YOLO allow-all except ask_user and Plan transition deny.

claims.caveat: User/admin policy layers can change effective behavior.

claims.claim: Policy decisions are allow, deny or ask_user with tiered precedence; Workspace policies are documented as currently non-functional.

sources.support: Official policy reference defines decisions, priority tiers and Workspace caveat.

claims.caveat: Effective policy depends on deployment configuration and mode.

claims.claim: Folder trust and MCP controls form separate permission layers: untrusted folders do not connect MCP; MCP execution checks folder trust + server trust or session server/tool allowlist; admin allow/block and user enablement can block servers.

sources.support: Trusted Folders guide lists restricted features including MCP connection.
MCP confirmation checks trusted folder/server trust and in-memory allowlist.
Manager blocks servers using allowed/blocked names and user session/file enablement.

claims.caveat: Trust/allowlist authorizes capability; it is not proof of successful external effect.

claims.claim: Telemetry and MessageBus/tool logging provide process observability when enabled, but do not by themselves prove business effect or an immutable audit trail.

sources.support: Official docs describe OTel logs/metrics/traces, local/GCP export and telemetry disabled by default.
State manager publishes TOOL_CALLS_UPDATE snapshots and terminal calls.

claims.caveat: No official end-to-end business outcome or tamper-evident audit guarantee was found.

claims.claim: Abort cancels scheduler calls/queued work and MCP tool races the call against AbortSignal; shell abort kills process groups, with tests verifying SIGTERM then SIGKILL; inactivity timeout yields cancellation messaging.

sources.support: Abort path marks calls cancelled and cancels queued calls.
MCP execute rejects AbortError on signal and cleans listener.
Official test asserts SIGTERM precedes SIGKILL on abort.
Timeout controller aborts and returns automatic cancellation message.

claims.caveat: Process termination does not prove remote side-effect rollback.

claims.claim: Network/model retry uses bounded attempts (default 10), backoff/jitter and selected transient errors; abort stops retry; 400 is not retried.

sources.support: Retry implementation defines default attempts, predicates, delay and signal checks.

claims.caveat: Retry of a request does not imply idempotent external tool execution.

claims.claim: Checkpointing is disabled by default and, when enabled, snapshots project files in shadow Git plus conversation/tool call before file modification; restore reverts that project/history scope and re-proposes the call.

sources.support: Official checkpoint guide states default off, snapshot contents and restore behavior.
Source serializes history, client history, tool call and commit hash; records snapshot failure.

claims.caveat: Does not establish rollback of remote/MCP/shell side effects or transactionality.

claims.claim: Official sources in this slice do not prove crash/disconnect deduplication, exactly-once, remote rollback or durable recovery of an uncertain tool result.
claims.caveat: This is a bounded absence-of-evidence finding: searched official docs, source and tests at the fixed commit; no guarantee that no such behavior exists elsewhere.

claims.claim: Official tests cover resume/checkpoint/context fidelity, but resume is not thereby proven to be a distributed exactly-once recovery protocol.

sources.support: Resume regression integration test.
Context fidelity on resume integration coverage.

claims.caveat: No crash-after-side-effect or duplicate suppression test was identified in this slice.

unresolved_conflicts: No direct source conflict was found; apparent tension between Plan Mode read-only docs and customizable policy is resolved by policy-layer caveat.
No official proof of exactly-once, crash recovery or remote rollback.
